summary: Checks whether a value is **not** an integer.
description: `nonInteger(value)` is the same test as `!isInteger(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
A number with no fractional part. Nothing is coerced, so the string `"42"` is not an integer, and `NaN` is not either.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not an integer; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonInteger(1.5); // => true
nonInteger(NaN); // => true
nonInteger("42"); // => true
nonInteger(42); // => false
nonInteger(-7); // => false
nonInteger(0); // => false
```
